projects.title: PocketBuddy
projects.shortDescription: A web and Android product that captures payments, forecasts allowance runway, coordinates shared purchases, and turns food and travel data into decisions.
projects.fullDescription: I built PocketBuddy end to end across a Kotlin Android connector, FastAPI and MongoDB services, a React interface, and AWS infrastructure. Deterministic code calculates runway and affordability before Amazon Bedrock writes short guidance from those facts. The product covers transaction capture, statement review, shared purchases, food routines, local travel, and privacy controls.
implementation: Built the complete web and mobile product, including the Kotlin connector, FastAPI services, MongoDB data layer, and React interface
Kept runway and affordability calculations deterministic, then constrained Bedrock Nova Lite to explain backend facts without inventing amounts or recommendations
Sent mobile events through API Gateway, Lambda, SQS, a dead-letter queue, and DynamoDB so retries remain traceable and duplicate transactions are rejected
Maintained 166 passing Python tests across payments, statement imports, privacy controls, forecasting, and shared purchases

projects.title: GitLore
projects.shortDescription: A service that turns pull requests, reviews, and repository history into searchable engineering decisions with cited answers and GitHub automation.
projects.fullDescription: Built with a four-person team at HackByte 4.0, GitLore converts GitHub pull-request history into a searchable knowledge graph. Engineers can ask why a decision was made, trace a line from blame to its pull request, and receive answers with source citations. The system spans a React web app, a Chrome extension, GitHub webhooks, and a Hono backend with more than 35 endpoints.
implementation: Mapped pull-request metadata, discussions, reviews, and webhooks into a searchable decision graph exposed through 35+ backend endpoints
Verified GitHub webhook signatures before duplicate-decision checks and kept draft-PR creation behind a user-triggered apply step
Protected routes with API-key and signed-cookie authentication and validated request bodies with Zod
Fell back from Atlas Vector Search to in-memory cosine, text, and regex search when indexes or embeddings were unavailable

projects.title: TinyRF-KD
projects.shortDescription: An edge intrusion-detection study that compresses a large random-forest teacher into KB-scale neural students, then checks explanations and microcontroller behavior.
projects.fullDescription: TinyRF-KD studies whether a strong tabular intrusion-detection teacher can be compressed for constrained hardware without hiding failures in class behavior, explanation agreement, or deployment. The work covers multi-seed evaluation on WSN-DS, SHAP faithfulness, fixed-point C export, and hardware-in-the-loop replay on ESP32-C3 and Arduino R4. The repository is public and the paper is still being written.
implementation: Compressed an 85,064 KB random-forest teacher into 4.64 KB and 13.27 KB neural students with 0.920 and 0.934 macro-F1 across 10 seeds
Measured a 0.047 Spearman correlation between global student and teacher SHAP rankings despite 98.69% and 98.91% student accuracy
Generated fixed-point C models with 1,348-byte and 3,700-byte parameter footprints
Replayed 56,200 test vectors on ESP32-C3 and Arduino R4 with 100% agreement against fixed-point reference outputs

projects.title: Covid-RARS
projects.shortDescription: A reliability study testing whether COVID respiratory-audio models survive participant, temporal, and cross-dataset shifts instead of only performing well in one split.
projects.fullDescription: Covid-RARS examines how respiratory-audio models behave when evaluation becomes stricter. It compares cough, breath, and speech pipelines on participant-disjoint and time-aware Coswara splits, then tests cough-only transfer to COUGHVID. The study also audits metadata shortcuts, feature stability, calibration, and decision utility. The repository is public and the paper is still being written.
implementation: Reached 0.895 AUROC and 0.862 AUPRC with validation-only cough-speech fusion on 314 participant-disjoint holdouts
Evaluated modality-matched transfer across 8,331 external COUGHVID recordings, where source AUROC of 0.849 to 0.868 fell to 0.523 to 0.543
Measured only 0.074 Jaccard overlap between early and late acoustic feature sets
Found a metadata-only model reaching 0.964 AUROC, exposing temporal instability and collection-context shortcuts

projects.title: ArthSaathi
projects.shortDescription: A mutual-fund analysis product that runs deterministic portfolio calculations through nine specialized agents and streams each stage to the interface.
projects.fullDescription: Built for the Economic Times GenAI Hackathon 2026, ArthSaathi turns mutual-fund CAS statements into an explainable portfolio report. Nine specialized agents parse the statement, enrich NAV data, calculate returns and costs, check overlap and benchmarks, project outcomes, score portfolio health, and prepare advice. Financial calculations stay deterministic while language models explain the computed results.
implementation: Orchestrated nine agents for CAS parsing, NAV enrichment, XIRR, overlap, TER, benchmark comparison, projections, portfolio scoring, and recommendations
Ran independent returns and overlap work concurrently with asyncio.gather and streamed start, progress, warning, and completion events through Server-Sent Events
Calculated portfolio metrics in deterministic Python code instead of asking a language model to produce financial values
Routed explanations through Claude, OpenAI, then Gemini, with a rule-based report when no provider returns usable content

projects.title: Uproot.AI
projects.shortDescription: A Next.js career-coaching application with resume and cover-letter tools, mock interviews, subscriptions, and account workflows.
projects.fullDescription: Uproot.AI brings resume drafting, cover-letter generation, interview practice, career guidance, and subscription management into one web application. It uses Next.js API routes with Prisma and PostgreSQL, plus external services for model calls, payments, file storage, email, and background jobs.
implementation: Implemented resume, cover-letter, interview-practice, and career-chat workflows in a Next.js application
Stored users, sessions, subscriptions, resumes, assessments, and usage records through Prisma and PostgreSQL
Connected Stripe for subscription state and Cloudinary for uploaded resume assets
Used Inngest and Resend for scheduled work and application email

projects.title: GlobeTrotter
projects.shortDescription: A multi-city trip planner with itinerary generation, budget breakdowns, calendar and timeline views, sharing, and administration tools.
projects.fullDescription: GlobeTrotter lets users create multi-city trips, generate and edit day-wise itineraries, estimate costs, review trips in calendar or timeline views, and share plans. A React client communicates with an Express API backed by MongoDB, with JWT and Google authentication and Cloudinary media storage.
implementation: Built trip creation, editing, sharing, and itinerary review flows across a React client and Express API
Added cost breakdowns and visual budget summaries for transport, stays, meals, and activities
Implemented email and Google sign-in, JWT sessions, password hashing, and profile management
Provided administration screens for users, cities, activities, and usage summaries

projects.title: W3nity
projects.shortDescription: A team prototype combining freelance listings, event registration, real-time community chat, wallet login, escrow, and NFT tickets.
projects.fullDescription: W3nity combines three hackathon modules in one application: a freelance marketplace, event management, and community chat. The React and TypeScript client connects to an Express and MongoDB backend, Socket.IO messaging, and Solidity contracts developed with Hardhat for escrow and ERC-721 tickets.
implementation: Connected freelance listings, proposals, event registration, and community channels through one React client
Used Socket.IO for public channels, direct messages, and message history
Developed Solidity contracts for escrow payments and ERC-721 event tickets with Hardhat
Integrated MetaMask wallet access through Wagmi and Ethers.js

projects.title: Hogwarts OS
projects.shortDescription: A team-built Linux Mint customization with themed desktop assets, command wrappers, small desktop tools, an assistant, and a Python game.
projects.fullDescription: Created for Hacknovate 6.0, Hogwarts OS packages themed Linux Mint customizations and installable modules rather than a new operating-system kernel. The repository includes Bash setup scripts, an Electron file explorer, Python tools, a spell-command wrapper, an assistant integration, and a Pygame mini-game.
implementation: Packaged themed boot, desktop, icon, sound, and login assets for Linux Mint Cinnamon
Mapped named commands to shell operations through a Bash command wrapper
Built installable modules including an Electron file explorer and Python desktop utilities
Added a Pygame mini-game and an external assistant integration for the hackathon demonstration

projects.title: UNI-TEL
projects.shortDescription: A student dashboard for semesters, subjects, attendance, marks, SGPA and CGPA calculations, and performance charts.
projects.fullDescription: UNI-TEL records semesters, subjects, credits, grades, attendance, and weighted marks in a Supabase-backed React application. It calculates SGPA and CGPA, presents performance charts, supports light and dark themes, and keeps each user’s academic records separated with Supabase authentication and row-level security.
implementation: Implemented semester, subject, credit, grade, attendance, and marks management
Calculated SGPA, CGPA, attendance percentages, and weighted scores from stored academic records
Rendered academic trends and summaries with Recharts
Applied Supabase authentication and row-level security to isolate user records

projects.title: NoobsterDSA
projects.shortDescription: A React and Supabase application for recording DSA practice, contest results, weekly goals, notes, and progress summaries.
projects.fullDescription: NoobsterDSA keeps daily problem-solving logs, contest records, and weekly goals in one interface. Users can attach topics, platforms, difficulty, time, notes, and resource links to entries, then review heatmaps, time distributions, and progress summaries.
implementation: Created daily logs for topics, solved problems, platforms, difficulty, time, notes, and resources
Added contest records, weekly goals, and written reflections
Built heatmaps, time-distribution charts, and progress summaries from the stored entries
Configured responsive and installable PWA behavior for desktop and mobile use

projects.title: BookSwap
projects.shortDescription: A campus Android application for book listings, timed auctions, image uploads, user accounts, and buyer-seller messaging.
projects.fullDescription: BookSwap is a Java Android application for listing and discovering books within a campus. Firebase Authentication manages accounts, Firestore stores listings and auctions, Realtime Database carries one-to-one messages, and Cloudinary stores uploaded book images.
implementation: Structured activities and fragments around an MVVM data flow with LiveData
Stored book listings and auction records in Cloud Firestore
Implemented buyer-seller chat through Firebase Realtime Database
Connected Firebase Authentication and Cloudinary image uploads to listing and profile flows
